title: Chronic Myeloid Leukemia
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2027)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2027 clinical navigator for Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (Chronic Phase, Accelerated Phase, Blast Phase). Implements Workup First diagnostic checklists (bone marrow karyotype for t(9;22), peripheral blood BCR::ABL1 qPCR on International Scale %IS, ELTS risk score calculation), 1L TKI selection (Imatinib vs 2G TKIs Dasatinib/Nilotinib/Bosutinib vs Asciminib STAMP inhibitor per ASC4FIRST trial), molecular milestones at 3/6/12 months, ABL1 kinase mutation gating, and T315I rescue with Ponatinib or high-dose Asciminib. References StewardMD ONCQIS Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Chronic Myeloid Leukemia Version 2.2027 (July 10, 2026).

a.text: ELTS (EUTOS Long-Term Survival) score is preferred over Sokal for 1L TKI selection: low risk 0.1611 x age is not used; score uses age, spleen size below costal margin, peripheral blast percentage, and platelet count. Cutoffs: low risk <=1.5680, intermediate 1.5680-2.2185, high >2.2185. High ELTS predicts inferior deep molecular response and CML-related death on imatinib, favoring a 2G TKI or asciminib.

b.text: ASC4FIRST trial: asciminib 80 mg daily (STAMP inhibitor Specifically Targeting the ABL Myristoyl Pocket) achieved superior major molecular response (MMR) at 48 weeks versus investigator-selected 1L TKI (imatinib or 2G TKI) in newly diagnosed CP-CML, with fewer discontinuations for adverse events. NCCN lists asciminib as a Category 1 first-line option.

c.text: Molecular milestones on the International Scale (%IS): BCR::ABL1 <=10% at 3 months, <=1% at 6 months, <=0.1% (MMR) at 12 months. Failure to meet milestones (ELN 2020 criteria adopted by NCCN) mandates adherence review, drug-interaction check, marrow cytogenetics, ABL1 kinase domain mutation testing, and TKI switch.

d.text: T315I gatekeeper mutation confers resistance to imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, and bosutinib. Active options are ponatinib (45 mg daily, dose-reduce on response per OPTIC) or asciminib 200 mg BID. Do not cycle to another standard-dose 2G TKI for T315I-positive disease.

e.text: OPTIC trial: ponatinib starting at 45 mg daily with mandatory reduction to 15 mg daily upon achieving BCR::ABL1 <=1% preserves response while reducing arterial occlusive events. Baseline and ongoing cardiovascular risk mitigation (blood pressure, lipids, HbA1c, smoking cessation, antiplatelet therapy when indicated) is required.

f.text: Allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) remains the only curative modality after TKI failure, for T315I-positive disease without deep response, and for AP/BP-CML. Initiate HLA typing and unrelated-donor search at first sign of resistance or at AP/BP diagnosis; refer early to a transplant center.

g.text: Comorbidity tailoring: avoid nilotinib with arterial occlusive disease, peripheral arterial disease, uncontrolled diabetes, hyperlipidemia, or QTc prolongation; avoid dasatinib with history of pleural effusion, pulmonary hypertension, or significant bleeding risk; avoid bosutinib with severe gastrointestinal or hepatic disease. Asciminib has a distinct tolerability profile but requires pancreatic enzyme and cardiovascular monitoring.

nodes.name: Disease Phase
nodes.title: CML: Disease Phase at Presentation
nodes.description: Step 1: Clinical Presentation. Assign CML phase from peripheral blood and bone marrow blast percentage, basophilia, platelet behavior, and clonal evolution. Phase determines whether the pathway is chronic-phase TKI selection or AP/BP intensification.
bullets: Chronic Phase (CP-CML): blasts <10% in blood and marrow, basophils usually <20%, Ph chromosome t(9;22)(q34.1;q11.2) with BCR::ABL1 p210 transcript in most patients.

Accelerated Phase (AP-CML): blasts 10-19% in blood or marrow, basophils >=20%, persistent thrombocytopenia (<100 x 10^9/L) or thrombocytosis (>1000 x 10^9/L) unresponsive to therapy, or clonal evolution with major-route additional cytogenetic abnormalities.
Blast Phase (BP-CML): blasts >=20% in blood or marrow, or extramedullary blast proliferation (myeloid sarcoma). Lineage (myeloid vs lymphoid) is assigned by flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry.
Confirm BCR::ABL1 positivity in every case before TKI initiation; BCR::ABL1-negative atypical CML follows a different pathway.

options.label: Chronic phase CML (CP-CML, blasts <10%)
Accelerated phase or blast phase CML (AP/BP-CML)

nodes.name: CP-CML Workup
nodes.title: CP-CML: Diagnostic Workup and Baseline Risk Assessment
nodes.description: Workup First: complete the diagnostic checklist establishing Ph status, baseline molecular burden, ELTS risk, and TKI-relevant comorbidities before selecting first-line therapy.
bullets: History and physical: spleen size in cm below costal margin (ELTS input), weight, B symptoms, bleeding or thrombotic history, full cardiovascular history including arterial occlusive disease and peripheral arterial disease, smoking status, pulmonary history (pleural effusion, pulmonary hypertension), gastrointestinal and hepatic history.
CBC with differential (blast %, basophil %, eosinophil %, platelet count), comprehensive metabolic panel with LFTs and renal function, LDH, uric acid.

Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy with conventional G-banding karyotype: confirm Ph chromosome t(9;22)(q34.1;q11.2), record percentage of Ph-positive metaphases, and screen for major-route additional cytogenetic abnormalities: trisomy 8 (+8), second Ph chromosome (+Ph), isochromosome 17q i(17q), and trisomy 19 (+19). Use FISH for BCR::ABL1 if karyotype is uninformative.

Quantitative RT-PCR (qPCR) for BCR::ABL1 on peripheral blood reported on the International Scale (%IS) as the treatment baseline; document transcript type (e13a2/e14a2 p210 typical; p190 or p230 atypical transcripts need assay-specific monitoring).
Calculate the ELTS (EUTOS Long-Term Survival) risk score from age, spleen size, peripheral blast %, and platelet count. ELTS is preferred over Sokal for 1L TKI selection.
Cardiovascular and metabolic assessment: baseline ECG for QTc interval, blood pressure, fasting lipid profile, HbA1c, ankle-brachial index if peripheral arterial disease is suspected.
ABL1 kinase domain mutation analysis is mandatory if there are AP/BP features, prior TKI exposure, or resistance; not routinely required in newly diagnosed CP-CML.
Serum pregnancy test in all patients of childbearing potential (TKIs are teratogenic); fertility counseling; hepatitis B screening before therapy; HLA typing discussion for high ELTS risk.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Risk Stratification & Therapy Selection

nodes.name: AP/BP-CML Workup
nodes.title: AP/BP-CML: Urgent Diagnostic Workup and Lineage Assignment
nodes.description: Workup First: AP/BP-CML is high risk for rapid progression. Complete lineage assignment, mutation profiling, CNS evaluation, and transplant workup without delaying TKI initiation.
bullets: CBC with differential, CMP with LFTs, LDH, uric acid, coagulation profile; tumor lysis laboratory panel (potassium, phosphate, calcium, creatinine) for blast-phase disease.

Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy with G-banding karyotype: confirm t(9;22)(q34.1;q11.2), quantify blast %, and identify major-route additional cytogenetic abnormalities (+8, +Ph, i(17q), +19) signifying clonal evolution.
Quantitative RT-PCR for BCR::ABL1 on peripheral blood on the International Scale (%IS); document transcript type.
ABL1 kinase domain mutation analysis is MANDATORY in AP/BP and before any TKI switch for resistance (gates T315I rescue with ponatinib or high-dose asciminib).
Lineage assignment by multiparameter flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry (myeloperoxidase, TdT, CD19, CD7, CD33, CD13) to distinguish myeloid from lymphoid blast phase.
CNS evaluation with diagnostic lumbar puncture for lymphoid BP (and for myeloid BP with neurologic symptoms); start CNS prophylaxis planning.
Baseline ECG (QTc), echocardiogram if anthracycline or intensive chemotherapy is anticipated, cardiovascular and metabolic assessment as for CP-CML.

Urgent HLA typing of patient and siblings plus unrelated-donor search initiation; early referral to transplant and leukemia centers; fertility counseling and pregnancy testing; leukapheresis only for symptomatic leukostasis, never as routine cytoreduction.
Calculate the ELTS (EUTOS Long-Term Survival) risk score from age, spleen size, peripheral blast %, and platelet count for baseline risk documentation.

options.label: Diagnostic Workup Reviewed — Proceed to Risk Stratification & Therapy Selection

nodes.name: ELTS Risk
nodes.title: CP-CML: ELTS Risk Stratification
nodes.description: ELTS score (age, spleen size, blast %, platelet count) stratifies CML-specific mortality and guides 1L TKI intensity: imatinib is acceptable in low risk, while intermediate/high risk favors a 2G TKI or asciminib.
bullets: ELTS low risk (score <=1.5680): imatinib 400 mg daily, any 2G TKI, or asciminib 80 mg daily are all appropriate; comorbidity profile and treatment-free-remission goals drive the choice.

ELTS intermediate risk (score 1.5680-2.2185): preferred 2G TKI (dasatinib, nilotinib, bosutinib) or asciminib (Category 1); imatinib is acceptable only if 2G TKI and asciminib are contraindicated or unavailable.
ELTS high risk (score >2.2185): preferred 2G TKI or asciminib (Category 1) for faster and deeper molecular responses; plan early milestone scrutiny and early donor-search discussion.
ELTS is preferred over Sokal and EUTOS scores for treatment selection in the TKI era.

options.label: ELTS low risk (score <=1.5680)
ELTS intermediate risk (score 1.5680-2.2185)
ELTS high risk (score >2.2185)

nodes.name: Comorbidity Profile
nodes.title: CP-CML: Comorbidity-Tailored TKI Selection
nodes.description: Match the 1L TKI to the patient's comorbidity profile. Each TKI has exclusionary toxicities: nilotinib (arterial occlusive, metabolic, QTc), dasatinib (pleural/pulmonary, bleeding), bosutinib (gastrointestinal, hepatic).
bullets: No major cardiopulmonary, metabolic, gastrointestinal, or hepatic comorbidity: full 1L menu is available (imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, bosutinib, asciminib); choose by ELTS risk, age, adherence considerations, and treatment-free-remission goals.

High cardiovascular, peripheral arterial, diabetic, or QTc risk: AVOID nilotinib; avoid ponatinib sequencing if possible; prefer imatinib, dasatinib, bosutinib, or asciminib with blood pressure, lipid, glucose, and ECG surveillance.

Pleural effusion history, pulmonary hypertension, chronic lung disease, or bleeding diathesis: AVOID dasatinib; prefer imatinib, nilotinib, bosutinib, or asciminib with chest imaging and echocardiography as indicated.
Severe gastrointestinal intolerance or hepatic dysfunction: AVOID bosutinib; prefer imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, or asciminib with LFT monitoring and antiemetic/antidiarrheal planning.
Review CYP3A4-mediated drug interactions, adherence barriers, pregnancy plans, and cost/access before final selection.

options.label: No major CV, pulmonary, GI, or hepatic comorbidity
High CV/PAD, diabetes, dyslipidemia, or QTc prolongation risk
Pleural effusion history, pulmonary hypertension, or bleeding risk
Severe GI intolerance or hepatic dysfunction

nodes.name: CP 1L Standard
nodes.title: CP-CML 1L Therapy: Full TKI Menu (No Major Comorbidity)
nodes.description: First-line TKI options when no exclusionary comorbidity exists. Low ELTS risk: imatinib, any 2G TKI, or asciminib. Intermediate/high ELTS risk: preferred 2G TKI or asciminib (Category 1).
bullets: Imatinib 400 mg PO daily with food and water (low ELTS risk option; monitor periorbital edema, fluid retention, muscle cramps, cytopenias, LFTs).
Dasatinib 100 mg PO daily (2G TKI; monitor for pleural effusion with chest imaging for respiratory symptoms, pulmonary hypertension, bleeding, QTc).
Nilotinib 300 mg PO BID on an empty stomach (2G TKI; monitor ECG QTc, fasting lipids and glucose, lipase, LFTs; counsel on arterial occlusive symptoms).
Bosutinib 400 mg PO daily with food (2G TKI; pre-empt diarrhea management, monitor LFTs monthly for 3 months then periodically).
Asciminib 80 mg PO daily, STAMP inhibitor, Category 1 per ASC4FIRST (preferred option including for intermediate/high ELTS risk; monitor pancreatic enzymes, blood pressure, lipids).
Counsel on lifelong adherence, CYP3A4 drug interactions, teratogenicity and contraception, and the 3/6/12-month molecular milestone schedule before starting.

options.label: 1L TKI started - proceed to molecular monitoring

nodes.name: CP 1L CV Risk
nodes.title: CP-CML 1L Therapy: High Cardiovascular/Metabolic Risk
nodes.description: First-line TKI options when arterial occlusive disease, peripheral arterial disease, diabetes, dyslipidemia, or QTc prolongation excludes nilotinib. Intermediate/high ELTS risk still favors dasatinib, bosutinib, or asciminib.
bullets: AVOID nilotinib (arterial occlusive events, peripheral arterial disease, hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, QTc prolongation, pancreatitis).
Imatinib 400 mg PO daily with food and water (safe cardiovascular profile; monitor fluid retention and cytopenias).
Dasatinib 100 mg PO daily with ECG and bleeding-risk review (acceptable cardiac profile at 100 mg daily; monitor pleural symptoms).
Bosutinib 400 mg PO daily with food (acceptable cardiovascular profile; monitor LFTs and diarrhea).
Asciminib 80 mg PO daily, STAMP inhibitor, Category 1 (preferred for intermediate/high ELTS risk with CV comorbidity; monitor blood pressure, lipids, pancreatic enzymes).
Institute aggressive CV risk mitigation at baseline: blood pressure control, statin therapy per lipid targets, HbA1c optimization, smoking cessation, baseline and periodic ECG.

options.label: 1L TKI started - proceed to molecular monitoring

nodes.name: CP 1L Pulmonary
nodes.title: CP-CML 1L Therapy: Pleural/Pulmonary or Bleeding Risk
nodes.description: First-line TKI options when pleural effusion history, pulmonary hypertension, chronic lung disease, or bleeding risk excludes dasatinib.
bullets: AVOID dasatinib (pleural effusion in up to one-third of patients over time, pulmonary arterial hypertension, platelet dysfunction and bleeding).
Imatinib 400 mg PO daily with food and water (monitor fluid retention and cytopenias; baseline chest imaging if prior effusion).
Nilotinib 300 mg PO BID fasting (monitor QTc, metabolic panel, vascular symptoms; requires CV risk review).
Bosutinib 400 mg PO daily with food (monitor LFTs and diarrhea; no pleural signal).
Asciminib 80 mg PO daily, STAMP inhibitor, Category 1 (preferred for intermediate/high ELTS risk with pulmonary comorbidity; monitor pancreatic enzymes).
Obtain baseline chest imaging and echocardiogram if pulmonary hypertension is suspected; hold TKI and evaluate any new dyspnea, cough, or chest pain promptly.

options.label: 1L TKI started - proceed to molecular monitoring

nodes.name: CP 1L GI Hepatic
nodes.title: CP-CML 1L Therapy: Severe GI or Hepatic Disease
nodes.description: First-line TKI options when severe gastrointestinal intolerance or hepatic dysfunction excludes bosutinib.
bullets: AVOID bosutinib (high rates of diarrhea, nausea, transaminitis; contraindicated with severe hepatic impairment).
Imatinib 400 mg PO daily with food and water (monitor LFTs, fluid retention, GI tolerance; dose-reduce for hepatic impairment per label).
Dasatinib 100 mg PO daily (monitor LFTs and GI tolerance; review pulmonary and bleeding history).
Nilotinib 300 mg PO BID fasting (monitor lipase, LFTs, bilirubin; fasting administration complicates GI tolerance counseling).
Asciminib 80 mg PO daily, STAMP inhibitor, Category 1 (preferred for intermediate/high ELTS risk with GI/hepatic comorbidity; monitor pancreatic enzymes and LFTs).
Check baseline LFTs, bilirubin, and albumin; repeat LFTs every 2 weeks for the first month then monthly; provide anticipatory antidiarrheal and antiemetic planning.

options.label: 1L TKI started - proceed to molecular monitoring

nodes.name: 3-Month Milestone
nodes.title: Molecular Monitoring: 3-Month Milestone (BCR::ABL1 %IS)
nodes.description: First molecular milestone on peripheral blood qPCR (International Scale). BCR::ABL1 <=10% IS is optimal; >10% IS is a warning requiring adherence review and closer surveillance, and failure (no hematologic or cytogenetic response) mandates switch.
bullets: Optimal: BCR::ABL1 <=10% IS at 3 months. Continue the same TKI and repeat qPCR at 6 months.
Warning: BCR::ABL1 >10% IS at 3 months. Verify adherence and CYP3A4 interactions, repeat qPCR in 1-3 months, obtain marrow cytogenetics and ABL1 kinase domain mutation testing.
Failure: no complete hematologic response or no cytogenetic response (Ph+ metaphases >95%) at 3 months. Switch TKI per mutation profile and evaluate for transplant.
Confirm the qPCR assay is IS-standardized before acting on a single value; repeat borderline results.

options.label: Optimal: BCR::ABL1 <=10% IS (continue same TKI)
Warning/Failure: BCR::ABL1 >10% IS or no cytogenetic response

nodes.name: 3-Month Warning Action
nodes.title: 3-Month Warning: Adherence, Interaction, and Mutation Workup
nodes.description: Structured rescue workup for BCR::ABL1 >10% IS at 3 months before the 6-month assessment: exclude non-biologic causes of poor response and genotype the clone.
bullets: Structured adherence review (pill counts, pharmacy refill data, dosing with food/fasting requirements, nilotinib BID spacing) and CYP3A4 inducer/inhibitor medication reconciliation.
Repeat peripheral blood qPCR on the International Scale in 4-12 weeks to confirm trajectory; do not switch on a single unconfirmed value unless failure criteria are met.
Bone marrow aspirate with karyotype to quantify Ph-positive metaphases and detect clonal evolution (major-route ACA).
ABL1 kinase domain mutation testing to gate the next TKI (T315I mandates ponatinib or high-dose asciminib).
If failure criteria are met (no CHR or Ph+ >95%), switch TKI immediately per mutation profile rather than waiting for 6 months.

options.label: Warning workup addressed - proceed to 6-month milestone

nodes.name: 6-Month Milestone
nodes.title: Molecular Monitoring: 6-Month Milestone (BCR::ABL1 %IS)
nodes.description: Second molecular milestone. BCR::ABL1 <=1% IS is optimal; >1% IS at 6 months is treatment failure requiring TKI switch per mutation testing.
bullets: Optimal: BCR::ABL1 <=1% IS at 6 months. Continue the same TKI and repeat qPCR at 12 months.
Warning zone: BCR::ABL1 1-10% IS at 6 months. Repeat adherence and interaction review, confirm with repeat qPCR, obtain mutation testing, and plan early switch if trajectory is flat or rising.
Failure: BCR::ABL1 >1% IS (and especially >10% IS) at 6 months. Switch TKI guided by ABL1 kinase domain mutation profile; initiate HLA typing and donor search.
Marrow cytogenetics if qPCR suggests failure, to document cytogenetic response depth and clonal evolution.

options.label: Optimal: BCR::ABL1 <=1% IS (continue same TKI)
Failure: BCR::ABL1 >1% IS (switch TKI per mutations)

nodes.name: 12-Month Milestone
nodes.title: Molecular Monitoring: 12-Month Milestone (MMR, BCR::ABL1 %IS)
nodes.description: Third molecular milestone. BCR::ABL1 <=0.1% IS (major molecular response, MMR, MR3.0) is optimal; >0.1% IS at 12 months is failure requiring switch.
bullets: Optimal: BCR::ABL1 <=0.1% IS (MMR, MR3.0) at 12 months. Continue the same TKI, space qPCR to every 3-6 months once MMR is stable, and track depth toward MR4.0/MR4.5 for future treatment-free-remission eligibility.
Failure: BCR::ABL1 >0.1% IS at 12 months. Switch TKI guided by ABL1 kinase domain mutation testing; marrow karyotype for clonal evolution; transplant evaluation for high-risk or multi-TKI failure.
Rising transcript on serial qPCR (e.g., 5-fold rise with loss of MMR) triggers the same resistance workup even between formal milestones.
Document MMR date: sustained deep molecular response for >=2 years on >=3 years of TKI is the gateway to a supervised treatment-free-remission attempt.

options.label: Optimal: BCR::ABL1 <=0.1% IS, MMR achieved
Failure: BCR::ABL1 >0.1% IS or loss of response

nodes.name: MMR Maintenance
nodes.title: MMR Achieved: Continue TKI, Long-Term Surveillance, TFR Planning
nodes.description: Optimal responders continue the tolerated TKI indefinitely with spaced molecular surveillance and long-term toxicity management; plan a supervised treatment-free-remission attempt once DMR criteria are met.
bullets: Continue the same TKI at the tolerated dose; do not de-escalate or stop outside a supervised treatment-free-remission protocol.
qPCR on the International Scale every 3 months until MMR is stable for 2 years, then every 3-6 months; marrow cytogenetics only if qPCR rises or response is lost.

Track depth of response (MR4.0 <=0.01%, MR4.5 <=0.0032%): eligibility for a treatment-free-remission attempt requires typically >=3 years of TKI and >=2 years of sustained deep molecular response, low-risk features, and close monthly qPCR monitoring after stopping.

Long-term TKI toxicity surveillance: annual cardiovascular and metabolic review (blood pressure, lipids, HbA1c, ECG QTc), pleural/pulmonary symptom review on dasatinib, LFTs on bosutinib/nilotinib, pancreatic enzymes on asciminib.
Maintain adherence counseling, CYP3A4 interaction review at every medication change, contraception during therapy, and bone health review for prolonged therapy.

nodes.name: Resistance Gating
nodes.title: Resistance: ABL1 Kinase Domain Mutation Gating
nodes.description: Milestone failure routes through ABL1 kinase domain mutation testing. T315I mandates ponatinib or high-dose asciminib; other mutations guide 2G TKI selection; no mutation triggers adherence/intolerance management and switch to a non-cross-resistant TKI.
bullets: Before labeling resistance: re-confirm adherence, CYP3A4 drug interactions, correct dosing and administration (nilotinib fasting, bosutinib with food), pregnancy, and IS-standardized repeat qPCR.
Obtain ABL1 kinase domain mutation analysis (NGS panel preferred to detect compound mutations) plus marrow karyotype for clonal evolution with major-route ACA.
T315I gatekeeper mutation: resistant to imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, and bosutinib; sensitive to ponatinib and asciminib. Prepare for allogeneic HCT.

Non-T315I mutations guide selection: Y253H, E255K/V, F359V/C/I favor dasatinib; F317L/V, T315A, V299L favor nilotinib; asciminib retains activity across most single mutants except select myristoyl-pocket variants.

No detectable mutation with milestone failure or intolerance: switch to an alternative TKI with a non-overlapping toxicity profile (asciminib preferred for multi-intolerance); recheck qPCR in 1-3 months.

options.label: T315I mutation detected (gatekeeper positive)
Non-T315I ABL1 mutation detected
No ABL1 mutation (adherence, interaction, or intolerance pattern)

nodes.name: T315I Rescue
nodes.title: T315I-Positive Resistance: Ponatinib or High-Dose Asciminib + HCT Planning
nodes.description: T315I rescue with the two active agents (ponatinib with OPTIC dose-reduction, or asciminib 200 mg BID) while preparing for allogeneic HCT.
bullets: Ponatinib 45 mg PO daily until BCR::ABL1 <=1% IS, then MANDATORY dose reduction to 15 mg PO daily (OPTIC response-adapted strategy); hold or reduce further for arterial occlusive symptoms, pancreatitis, hepatotoxicity, or severe cytopenias.
Alternative: asciminib 200 mg PO BID (STAMP inhibitor active against T315I including compound-mutant clones; monitor pancreatic enzymes, blood pressure, lipids).
Do NOT cycle to imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, or bosutinib for T315I-positive disease (uniform resistance).

Cardiovascular risk mitigation is mandatory on ponatinib: baseline and serial blood pressure, lipid, HbA1c, and ECG monitoring; smoking cessation; antiplatelet therapy when not contraindicated; cardiology co-management for high-risk patients.
Initiate HLA typing and unrelated-donor search immediately; refer to a transplant center; qPCR every 1-3 months until deep response, then per maintenance schedule.

nodes.name: Non-T315I Switch
nodes.title: Non-T315I Resistance: Mutation-Guided TKI Switch
nodes.description: Second/third-line TKI selected from the ABL1 mutation profile: dasatinib- or nilotinib-sensitive mutants route to the active 2G TKI; multi-resistant or compound mutants route to asciminib or ponatinib.
bullets: Y253H, E255K/V, F359V/C/I mutants: switch to dasatinib 100-140 mg PO daily (review pleural, pulmonary, and bleeding history first).
F317L/V, T315A, V299L mutants: switch to nilotinib 400 mg PO BID (review cardiovascular, metabolic, and QTc status first).

Multi-resistant, compound, or uncharacterized mutants: asciminib (standard dose per label; 200 mg BID if T315I co-mutation emerges) or ponatinib 45 mg daily with OPTIC dose-reduction and cardiovascular mitigation.
Bosutinib 500 mg PO daily is an option for resistance without a dasatinib/nilotinib-sensitive mutation when GI and hepatic tolerance allow.
Marrow karyotype at switch for clonal evolution; HLA typing and donor search for second failure, high ELTS risk, or AP/BP features; qPCR every 1-3 months until milestones are re-achieved.

nodes.name: Intolerance Switch
nodes.title: No Mutation: Adherence Rescue and Intolerance Switch
nodes.description: Milestone failure without an ABL1 mutation is most often adherence, interaction, or intolerance: remediate the cause and switch to a TKI with a non-overlapping toxicity profile rather than escalating dose.
bullets: Complete adherence rescue: dosing education (nilotinib fasting and BID spacing, bosutinib with food), pill organizer or reminder system, pharmacy refill reconciliation, and CYP3A4 medication review.

Manage grade 1-2 toxicities with dose holds and label-directed dose reductions before abandoning an effective TKI; use antiemetics, antidiarrheals, diuretics, and topical or systemic steroids per toxicity type.

For persistent intolerance, switch to a TKI with a non-overlapping toxicity profile: asciminib is preferred after multiple intolerances given its distinct STAMP-mechanism tolerability; otherwise select per the comorbidity matrix (avoid nilotinib in CV risk, dasatinib in pleural risk, bosutinib in GI/hepatic disease).
Recheck qPCR in 1-3 months after switch; if milestones remain unmet, repeat ABL1 mutation testing (clonal selection can emerge) and proceed to the resistance pathway.
Document intolerance grade, attribution, and resolution to guide future sequencing and transplant discussions.

nodes.name: AP/BP Assignment
nodes.title: AP/BP-CML: Phase and Lineage Assignment
nodes.description: Assign accelerated phase versus myeloid or lymphoid blast phase from blast percentage, lineage immunophenotyping, and extramedullary disease. Each assignment has a distinct chemo-immunotherapy backbone added to TKI therapy.
bullets: Accelerated phase (blasts 10-19%, basophils >=20%, refractory cytoses/cytopenias, or clonal evolution): potent TKI (2G TKI, ponatinib, or asciminib per mutation profile) with donor search and planned allogeneic HCT.
Myeloid blast phase (>=20% myeloid blasts or myeloid sarcoma): TKI plus AML-type induction (cytarabine/anthracycline 7+3 backbone) followed by allogeneic HCT.
Lymphoid blast phase (>=20% lymphoblasts, TdT/CD19 positive): TKI plus ALL-type induction (Hyper-CVAD backbone with steroids and vincristine) plus CNS prophylaxis, followed by allogeneic HCT.
Start or continue TKI immediately at AP/BP recognition; do not delay TKI while awaiting full lineage workup.

options.label: Accelerated phase CML (AP-CML)
Myeloid blast phase CML (myeloid BP)
Lymphoid blast phase CML (lymphoid BP)

nodes.name: AP Treatment
nodes.title: AP-CML: Potent TKI + Donor Search + Planned Allogeneic HCT
nodes.description: Accelerated-phase therapy with a potent TKI selected by mutation profile, close surveillance for blast progression, and transplant planning.
bullets: Start a potent TKI immediately: dasatinib 100-140 mg daily, nilotinib 400 mg BID, bosutinib 500 mg daily, ponatinib 45 mg daily (with OPTIC reduction), or asciminib per label, selected by ABL1 mutation profile and comorbidity matrix; T315I mandates ponatinib or asciminib 200 mg BID.
HLA typing and unrelated-donor search at diagnosis; early referral to a transplant center with intent for allogeneic HCT, particularly for clonal evolution, T315I, or incomplete response.
Monitor CBC and qPCR every 1-3 months with marrow karyotype until response; any rise to >=20% blasts reclassifies as blast phase and switches to BP therapy.
Consider clinical trial enrollment; single-agent TKI may suffice for AP-CML achieving rapid deep response, with HCT reserved for inadequate responders.
Manage TKI toxicities per the comorbidity matrix with cardiovascular, pleural, GI, and hepatic surveillance as in CP-CML.

nodes.name: Myeloid BP Treatment
nodes.title: Myeloid BP-CML: TKI + AML Induction, Then Allogeneic HCT
nodes.description: Myeloid blast-phase therapy combining a potent TKI (dasatinib or ponatinib preferred) with AML-type 7+3 induction, followed by allogeneic HCT in responders.
bullets: TKI backbone: dasatinib 140 mg PO daily or ponatinib 45 mg PO daily (with OPTIC dose-reduction and cardiovascular mitigation), selected by mutation profile; continue TKI through induction.

AML-type induction: cytarabine plus anthracycline 7+3 backbone (idarubicin or daunorubicin per fitness and cardiac function); tumor lysis prophylaxis with hydration, allopurinol or rasburicase, and electrolyte monitoring.
CNS assessment with lumbar puncture; intrathecal prophylaxis for high-risk or CNS-positive disease.
Reassess marrow after induction: responders proceed to allogeneic HCT without delay; primary refractory disease warrants FLAG-IDA or similar salvage per the AML pathway plus trial consideration.
Aggressive supportive care: febrile neutropenia protocols, transfusion thresholds, antifungal prophylaxis, growth factor per institutional policy.

nodes.name: Lymphoid BP Treatment
nodes.title: Lymphoid BP-CML: TKI + ALL Induction + CNS Prophylaxis, Then Allogeneic HCT
nodes.description: Lymphoid blast-phase therapy combining a potent TKI with ALL-type Hyper-CVAD-based induction, steroids, and mandatory CNS prophylaxis, followed by allogeneic HCT.
bullets: TKI backbone: dasatinib 140 mg PO daily (excellent CNS penetration) or ponatinib 45 mg PO daily for T315I-positive disease, continued through ALL induction and maintenance.

ALL-type induction: Hyper-CVAD backbone (hyperfractionated cyclophosphamide, vincristine, doxorubicin, dexamethasone alternating with high-dose methotrexate and cytarabine) with corticosteroid pre-phase per fitness.
Mandatory CNS prophylaxis: intrathecal methotrexate and cytarabine alternating during induction regardless of baseline CSF status; therapeutic intrathecal schedule if CSF positive.
Reassess marrow and MRD after induction: responders proceed to allogeneic HCT; consider blinatumomab-based bridging for persistent lymphoid MRD per the ALL pathway.
Tumor lysis prophylaxis, hepatitis B monitoring on steroids and chemotherapy, fertility preservation discussion before induction when feasible.
